classification_reasons: check_ratchets is wired into CHECKS_BY_PHASE for (c), (d) and (e) for every change_type in every project the plugin drives (intent.md 'Affected users and systems'); an always-on gate addition is a wide blast radius even though it is additive and no existing check's signature changes.

Two non-obvious design choices carry real evasion risk if read the other way: declaration is checked against ctx.approved_artifact('plan.md') at the merge base rather than the working tree (so a commit cannot excuse its own drop by editing plan.md alongside it), and the dot-prefixed-rename rule for eval cases is evaluated independently of the survivor-emptiness rule (panel decision #1) so a surviving sibling cannot be used to hide a renamed-to-hidden case. Both are pinned by dedicated tests, but both are the kind of inversion a future edit could silently undo.

All coverage is new, not pre-existing: every behavior (drop rules, declaration paths, acceptance, skip-marker scan, unpark union, PR clause) is proved by tests written in this same change (plan.md's own interrogation answer 5 confirms no claim of pre-existing coverage).
attempted: Intent: the diff matches intent.md's Proposed outcome point for point - a ratchets check at (c)/(d)/(e) for every change type, dropped-test and dropped-eval-case rules with rename/dot-rename handling, plan-declared exemptions, a risk-list-shaped undeclared hit, skip-marker listing, reviewer/REVIEW.md angles, and a version bump. Nothing solves a nearby but different problem.

Spec and plan: cross-read spec.md's Requirements/Design/Acceptance against plan.md's Files-that-change, Order of work and Proof - every named file is touched in the stated order, every Acceptance case has a correspondingly named test in tests/test_gate.py, test_state.py, test_pr.py, test_agents.py, test_commands_and_skills.py and test_templates.py, and all of intent.md's and spec.md's Flagged concerns are closed with a decision (no open [ ] remains). plan.md's own riskiest-step mitigation (merge-base plan read) and the eval-case survivor-vs-drop gap are both present as dedicated tests, matching the Risks section's own account.

Proof: read the actual diff for plugin/gate/diff.py, plugin/gate/checks.py (check_ratchets, dropped_test_files, dropped_eval_cases, skip_marker_hits, _declared_ratchets), plugin/state/unpark.py and plugin/pr/description.py directly, plus the new tests in tests/test_gate.py/test_state.py/test_pr.py; traced the probe='{path}.' trick against hooks/plan_sync.py's is_planned to confirm the directory-with-trailing-slash match actually works (changed.strip('/') would otherwise eat the trailing slash and break a direct comparison - the probe avoids that). test.log/build.log/lint.log for phase (d) read '# <command> - deferred to the runner', which per the plugin's own CI-session convention (issue #91, item 3b) is not missing proof; the committed gate-c.json already carries the runner's real build/test/lint output (1694 passed, exit 0 all three) from the same code this diff carries forward unchanged into phase (d), and verifier.md documents direct exercise of every new pure function against spec.md's Acceptance cases. Did not cite or rely on any evidence/claude-*.json, run-*.json or status.yaml gate record as proof for or against the diff.

Blast radius: no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml) is touched by the diff; the one guardrail-adjacent edit (this repo's own root REVIEW.md) is correctly left to the owner via a docs/PROGRESS.md table row, never written directly. check_ratchets is additive to CHECKS_BY_PHASE with no change to any existing check's signature or call site, so no other caller (gate CLI, run_phase.py's guard, the panel's fixed items list) needs a change. Confirmed the new check is absent from CHECKS_BY_PHASE['a']/['b']/['f'] per spec, and (correctly, by design) absent from this very change's own gate-c.json run since the build gate itself executes against the pinned framework/ checkout, not this diff's own plugin/ copy - spec.md's flagged concern names this scope boundary explicitly and the diff does not touch framework/.

Policies: security-baseline's no-shell-string/no-shell=True rule is honoured (diffmod._git's argument-list convention, -M named explicitly); data-conventions does not apply (no stored field or personal data, just source-tree paths already in git history); coding-standards rule 4 (no weakened/deleted test) holds - no existing test's assertions were removed.

Tests: found that tests/test_templates.py's new test_review_md_skip_marker_rule_present is spliced into the middle of the pre-existing test_review_md_structure body (three of that function's original assertions - about .claude/**, the test-file-lock bullet and plan.md conformance - now run under the new function's name instead). This is a genuine sloppy-edit smell, but it does not weaken coverage (every assertion still runs and still passes) and it was already surfaced and explicitly accepted as a non-Important nit by the phase (c) adversarial review (round-4 fix response, 2026-10-16) with the same reasoning; re-confirmed here rather than re-litigated. No test in the diff could pass with the described bug present: the drop-rule and declaration tests assert on concrete details.hits/details.declared values that only the correct logic produces, and the dot-rename-vs-survivor test and the partial-delete test pin opposite outcomes that a records-only or survivor-only implementation could not both satisfy.
